text:
Calgary arrives in Las Vegas having conceded 4.83 goals a game through six outings, and the chance numbers suggest that is not just bad luck. The Flames create 2.93 expected goals per 60 minutes but allow 3.24, and they hold just 49 percent of the 5-on-5 chance share. Vegas runs the other way, creating 3.49 per 60 and allowing 2.45, with a 56 percent share. The model projects 3.59 goals for the Golden Knights and 2.67 for Calgary.

Special teams widen the gap. Vegas generates 0.85 power-play expected goals a night and gives up 0.34 on the penalty kill, and it draws 4.75 penalties a game against 3.38 taken. Calgary is at 0.28 on the power play and 0.46 against on the kill, while taking 4.67 penalties a game, which is a lot of time to hand an opponent with that kind of power play. In goal, Dustin Wolf (projected) has a .840 save percentage and is 6.07 goals worse than expected over four games, after finishing 2.8 below expected across 57 games last season. Carter Hart (projected) sits at .910 and 0.64 goals above expected, though he was 4.44 below over 18 games last year.

Form leans Vegas, which has taken points in four of its last five and put up the better chance share in three of them, even in the 4-2 loss at Minnesota. Calgary has lost four of five, and its one win, 4-2 at Anaheim on Tuesday, came with a 62 percent chance share, its best of the stretch. Among the players the model likes, Mark Stone (36 percent to score), Jack Eichel (34) and Tomas Hertl (32) lead Vegas, with Eichel at 38 percent for two or more points. For Calgary, Morgan Frost, Joel Farabee and Mikael Backlund each sit at 23 percent to score.
